Synopsis:
Mexico's annual headline inflation accelerated to 3.26% in August (from 3.12% in July), breaking a five-month easing trend, though slightly below the 3.3% Reuters poll forecast. Core inflation showed signs of relief, decelerating to 3.88% annually and 0.16% monthly — both below expectations. Banxico's Deputy Governor signaled no near-term rate cuts, with further easing potentially ~1 year away. Food price volatility, El Niño risks, and persistent services inflation keep the policy stance cautious. Mexico's government projects inflation at 3.5% end-2026 and 3.0% end-2027.
